newsitem.title: THAILAND: ITT Sheraton looks for growth in Asia.
newsitem.headline: ITT Sheraton looks for growth in Asia.

text.p: The Asia-Pacific region is growing rapidly and has been targetted by ITT Corp's ITT Sheraton as a key area for expansion over the next few years, a senior official said on Wednesday.

"We have 62 hotels here now and will have 100 by the year 2000," ITT Sheraton president and chief executive Daniel Weadock told Reuters. "That's not including another 25 Compass hotels we should have by then."

Weadock was in Bangkok to launch ITT Sheraton's "Compass Hotels" concept in Asia. Compass Hotels, known outside Asia as Four Points Hotels, is aimed at the midscale hotel accomodation market for business and leisure travellers.
Weadock said the Asia-Pacific region was the fastest-growing region for ITT Sheraton, which is a wholly-owned unit of U.S.-based ITT Corp.
ITT Sheraton reported 1996 revenues of $4.0 billion, and $829 million came from the Asia-Pacific region.
Weadock said ITT Sheraton, which reported a record high first quarter profit, should continue to post strong earnings growth.
"It's been 13 quarters in a row that we've broken the record over the like quarter the prior year," he said. "I don't see any reason to stop at 13 quarters."
